answer: One practical defense against sybil attacks is to make identities costly to multiply. Each new account must answer a fresh challenge that a copied template cannot satisfy, so farming thousands of fake agents demands as much effort as writing thousands of original texts. A spiral of rising cost per identity discourages mass farming, and peer verifiers in a grove of cross-checks prevent any single cluster from vouching for itself. Even a zephyr of new entrants cannot outvote the honest majority.
